---
title: "Analytical Assurance Decision Tool"
description: "Score impact and likelihood to find the level of assurance needed."
---

**All analysis shall be assured.** How much assurance depends on the work.

The [Analytical Assurance Decision Tool spreadsheet]({{< var decision-tool >}}) sets your assurance level. It holds the scales for each dimension. Opening it needs an NHSBSA account with access
to the Analytical Quality and Assurance site.

Score the impact, score the likelihood, and read your level where the two scores meet.

## What you do

The picture shows when each step happens, for work where no impact dimension scores Level 4 and for work where one does.

{{< include /guidance/_partials/diagram-assurance-level-timing.qmd >}}

| Step | What you do |
|---|---|
| **1. [Score the impact](score-the-impact.qmd)** | Score six dimensions with your commissioner, Level 1 to Level 4. Take your highest single level. A Level 4 on any dimension makes the work Business Critical |
| **2. [Score the likelihood](score-the-likelihood.qmd)** | Score six dimensions, Level 1 to Level 4. Take your highest single level. Score once the data and the method are settled |
| **3. [Read your level](read-your-level.qmd)** | Find where your two scores meet on the matrix |
| **4. [Do what your level requires](what-your-level-requires.qmd)** | Read the column for your level, then do every check up to it |

: The four steps and what you do in each

If an impact dimension scored 4, go to [Business Critical analysis](../08-business-critical/index.qmd).

## Rules for scoring

- Take the highest single score. Do not average.
- If two answers both look defensible, take the higher.
- Record each score when you make it. If circumstances change, change the score and record why.
- Before you reuse the work for a new purpose, run [the four checks before reuse](../05-review/index.qmd#check-four-things-before-any-reuse). Score again if any answer is yes.
- Score an output that runs to a schedule once, when you design it. Do not rescore it on every
  run.
- Check the level at [Phase 5, review](../05-review/index.qmd). Score again sooner if the data,
  the method, the audience or the decision it informs changes.

## Outputs of setting your level

Record these in the Specification:

- At scoping: the impact score and the Business Critical answer, yes or no.
- At scoping: the acceptable level of risk, and the levels of quality and certainty required.
- At design: the finished level of assurance, added before the assurance plan.
- For Level 4 BCA, at scoping: the finished level and the completed tool.

## Three prompts to answer while the tool is open {#three-prompts-that-do-not-change-the-level}

Ask these three questions while the tool is open.

- **Is an algorithmic or machine learning tool doing part of the work?** If so, [check whether your tool needs a transparency record](../09-resources/r12-algorithmic-transparency-and-ai.qmd#check-whether-your-tool-needs-a-transparency-record).
- **Will this output influence the same kind of decision repeatedly?**
- **Could any group be affected differently by the decision this informs?** If yes, record it in
  the six-field record in [data ethics and personal data](../09-resources/r11-ethics-and-personal-data.qmd).

None of them raises the level by itself. A yes to any of them might change what you design.

## Models, limited time and disagreements

For a model, limited time or a disagreement about the level, see
[After you have your level](after-you-have-your-level.qmd).
